cells.tense: You are here with the ink still wet, writing the next moment as it arrives.
cells.ask: When someone says something you didn't expect, follow it a little. Ask one real question and let the answer take you somewhere you didn't plan to go.
cells.core:
You can meet someone without deciding in advance what they are. That's rarer than it sounds. Most people walk in carrying a script for the other person, and you're not — you're just there, able to be surprised by what's actually in front of you.

When it's going well, that openness pulls you toward what's worth moving toward. The connection itself sets the direction, and you follow it because it's real and not something you adopted to feel better. When you catch yourself speaking from something already assembled about the person across from you, that's the signal. Put it down. The next true thing shows up in the space it leaves.

cells.place: in the connection between you and whoever is across from you

cells.tense: You are living ahead of the moment, bracing for a version of the connection that hasn't arrived.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you've been holding open with someone and close it — a plan, a decision, a yes or a no. Say the plain version today, without routing it through what it might become.
cells.core:
You keep every version of the connection alive at once. The one where it goes well, the one where they understand you, the one that finally turns into something — and because none of them have been let go, none of them are real yet. The person in front of you gets met as a possibility instead of a person.

When this is steady, the pull forward comes from what's genuinely grown between you, and the connection shows that without effort. What it costs to keep it is that nothing becomes actual. Let a choice land and see what the two of you are once one version has room to breathe.

cells.tense: You are still standing at a door that closed a long time behind you.
cells.ask: In a conversation with someone familiar, tell them one thing you noticed and liked about them, with the detail that makes it true. Let that small true thing reach them.
cells.core:
You catch people accurately and the catch doesn't reach anyone. You can read a room, see exactly where someone is, and still let the moment pass without any of it landing between you and them.

When you are open, you know before you decide what you're dealing with, and nothing has been collapsed yet. There is a place in this connection only belief can build, and it's the kind of thing made from small, specific moments — a detail you notice, said out loud, that no one else would have caught. What it costs to stay shut is that the person never finds out you saw them. A feeling isn't the thing to summon here, and it isn't a wound to describe. It's a detail you let land in a room you're already in.

cells.tense: The door is right there and your hand is already on it, but you talk like someone still deciding whether to go in.
cells.ask: Name one way you've been with someone this week that came from your own intent, not from handling them. Say what you did, even if you can't say why.
cells.core:
You are already shaping what happens between you and other people — in what you say, what you let pass, where you turn toward them — and you describe it as if the situation were doing the deciding. The connection gets made and you keep meeting people as people to manage instead of people you are choosing.

When this is awake, the pull toward someone comes from ground you already have under you, and it doesn't need to be proven first. Staying reactive closes the field where something new could have been. Say what you did. Give yourself a little of the credit, and next time there's more room.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is that a person running sealed comes from a specific old refusal; the record only lets me place a door behind them, not say what stood there. A reader could reasonably object that they are simply careful with people, not closed, so the Too Little cell is written to describe the missing sorting, not a verdict about history. The ask survives being wrong: even a guarded person can let one unfamiliar detail land, and nothing in it demands an account of what happened. The sentence that serves me is 'every room comes with a read already attached' — it sounds sharp but outruns what the record supports; the card says the text stays open, not that the person closes it.
